subject: Proposed proportional discount framework + transition plan
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>

Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Bridging from modular to metered pricing – how to make it fair

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the throughput guarantees on Redwood Dedicated. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask: Acme wants to move from our current modular seat-based bundle to a more metered, per-token model, but we need a predictable way to transition without taking a big P&L hit the first 6 months.

Can you outline options for:
- a phased transition (mixed billing)
- crediting unused seat commitments against metered consumption
- an introductory discount schedule that scales down over time

We also need a short doc we can share with finance. Can you send an outline and a sample math sheet?

Thanks,
Julia
Julia Park
Head of Product Operations, Acme Health
julia.park@acmehealth.com

Attachment: none
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmehealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridging from modular to metered pricing – how to make it fair

Julia —

Appreciate the clear ask. I put together two pragmatic paths and a short example sheet (attached):

Option A — Proportional bridge (recommended for predictable cost smoothing)
- Convert committed seats to a time-phased credit that applies to metered tokens for the first 6 months.
- Example: 12 months remaining on seat commitment -> 50% of remaining monthly commitment converts to a token credit for months 1–6, then steps down to 25% months 7–12.
- Intro discount: 25% on metered rate for month 1, tapering 5 percentage points each subsequent month.

Option B — Dual-bill pilot (recommended for low-risk validation)
- Keep seat billing for a capped baseline, meter consumption above baseline.
- Short pilot (90 days) to measure steady-state token consumption, then negotiate final conversion.

Attachments included: PlanBridge-v1.pdf (explanatory flow + policy), MA-Redwood-Acme-Proposal.xlsx (sample math).

If agreed, we can run a short workshop with your finance team to populate the actual commitment numbers and produce a final schedule. Lauren — should we propose a one-hour workshop next week? Ben — FYI on discount shaping and margin impact.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Attachments: PlanBridge-v1.pdf, MA-Redwood-Acme-Proposal.xlsx
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-23T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridging from modular to metered pricing – how to make it fair

Sofia — quick internal notes before we finalize the doc for Acme:

- Commercial guardrails: avoid >40% effective discount in year-1 on expected token run-rate. If customer consumption ends up >150% of forecast, we should pause credits and reprice.
- Contract language: include a defined step-down schedule and an audit clause for usage verification (30-day review cycles).
- Accounting: structure credits as bill-time offsets (not refunds) to keep revenue recognition cleaner for both sides.

Ben — would you run the attached sample sheet against the Acme numbers Sofia has? I flagged three places where margin compression gets steep (lots of small prompts + long context usage).

Lauren
VP, Revenue Operations
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-27T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Bridging from modular to metered pricing – how to make it fair

Hi Julia —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a short proposal and a worked example that implements the proportional bridge we discussed. High-level summary:

- 6-month bridge credits equal to 50% of the remaining seat value, applied monthly against metered consumption.
- Intro metered discount schedule: 25% month 1, 20% month 2, 15% month 3, then 10% months 4–6.
- Dual-bill pilot variant included if you prefer a gradual floor during measurement.
- Audit & cadence: monthly usage review for the first 6 months; trigger to reprice if consumption >150% of forecast for two consecutive months.

Next steps: please confirm which path (A — proportional bridge vs B — dual-bill pilot) you prefer and share a date/time for the finance workshop. If helpful, we can draft the contract language for the credit schedule and the audit clause to speed procurement.

Best regards,
Sofia
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Attachments: PlanBridge-v1.pdf, MA-Redwood-Acme-Proposal.xlsx
